Q1: Polyaminopropyl biguanide exhibits known significant hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or reproductive effects (CMR), environmental impact (ENV), and oral exposure (ORL). However, its hazard profile is data deficient (Tier 4) for endocrine disruption (EDC), inhalation hazards (IHL), dermal and eye hazards (SKN), and organ and systemic hazards (OGN).
Q2: This chemical is not currently on any specified "Lists of Concern." This absence may be due, in part, to significant data deficiencies across several hazard classes, suggesting a lack of comprehensive study in certain areas.
Q3: With 469 literature references, Polyaminopropyl biguanide has a moderate level of study compared to other chemicals. Its well-defined polymeric molecular formula, (C5H14N6)x, and substance class do not indicate an incompletely characterized material; however, five data-deficient (Tier 4) hazard classifications highlight significant gaps in its hazard profile for endocrine disruption, inhalation, dermal/eye, and organ/systemic effects.
